subject.title: [Feature]: GitHub Copilot provider cannot reach GitHub Enterprise data-residency (*.ghe.com) tenants

question: Should the bundled github-copilot provider accept allowlisted GitHub Enterprise data-residency tenant routing, including config/env host selection and domain-scoped token caches?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested tenant path, but the fix changes an auth-provider security boundary and adds provider setup surface, so automation cannot decide the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Accept bounded bundled-provider routing
options.body: Review and harden the linked PR as the supported way for the existing github-copilot provider to handle github.com and single-label *.ghe.com tenants without changing public GitHub defaults.

options.title: Route GHE Copilot outside core
options.body: Reject bundled-provider tenant routing and require a separate plugin or ClawHub package if maintainers want enterprise-specific Copilot behavior outside the bundled provider.

options.title: Require a generic host-routing contract first
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers define a reusable provider-auth tenant-host API instead of a provider-specific config and SDK surface.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded bundled-provider routing
recommendation.body: Review and harden the linked PR as the supported way for the existing github-copilot provider to handle github.com and single-label *.ghe.com tenants without changing public GitHub defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent current-main history across the provider/auth/runtime files that would carry this decision.
